examples.ko: 학교가 재정난 때문에 도서관 공사를 미뤘어요.
examples.en: The school postponed the library construction because of financial difficulties.
Small shops are going through financial difficulties.

examples.ko: 시청은 재정난이 심해져서 행사를 줄이기로 했어요.
examples.en: The city hall's finances got so bad that it decided to cut back on events.

examples.ko: 회사가 재정난에 빠져서 월급이 늦게 나와요.
examples.en: The company is in financial trouble, so salaries come late.

examples.ko: 재정난으로 문을 닫는 병원이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More hospitals are closing because of financial trouble.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리도 재정난을 이겨내려고 회비를 올렸어요.
examples.en: Our club also raised its fees to get through the money shortage.

explain: '-난'은 '구인난', '주택난', '전력난'처럼 무언가가 모자라서 어려운 상황을 나타내요. 재정난은 나라, 회사, 학교, 단체의 돈 문제에 주로 쓰고, 개인은 '돈이 없다', '형편이 어렵다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 재정난에 빠져서 직원을 줄였어요.
phrases.en: The company fell into financial difficulty and cut staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상태가 시작되거나 깊어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a difficult state begins or deepens.

phrases.en: The city tries to solve its financial difficulty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 풀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for solving the problem.

phrases.en: These days our school has serious financial difficulties.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움이 크다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe that the difficulty is severe.

explain_en: The ending '-난' marks a difficult situation caused by a shortage, as in '구인난', '주택난' and '전력난'. 재정난 is mostly used for the money problems of countries, companies, schools and groups; for individuals people say '돈이 없다' or '형편이 어렵다'.

t90.ax: Small shops are going through financial difficulties.

examples.en: Rainfall is expected tonight.
There was little rainfall this year, so water is short.
The weather agency announced a regional rainfall forecast.
The baseball game was canceled because of rain.
A lot of rainfall was recorded in the mountains.
When the rain stops, the road will dry.

explain: '강우'는 비가 내리는 것을 날씨 뉴스에서 부르는 말이에요. 평소에는 그냥 '비'라고 하고, 비가 온 양은 '강우량'이라고 해요. 눈이 오는 것은 '강설', 비와 눈을 합쳐서는 '강수'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This month's rainfall is higher than usual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 내린 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the amount of rain that fell.

phrases.example: 내일 강우 예보가 있어서 우산을 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: Rain is forecast for tomorrow, so I brought an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 올 것이라는 날씨 소식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weather news saying rain is coming.

phrases.en: There is a lot of rainfall in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 많이 오는 때나 곳을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a time or place with a lot of rain.
phrases.en_equiv: there is a lot of rainfall

explain_en: 강우 is the word weather reports use for rain falling. In daily life people just say 비, and the amount of rain is 강우량. Snowfall is 강설, and rain and snow together are called 강수.

examples.en: A strong earthquake hit Japan and buildings shook.

examples.ko: 강진 뒤에는 여진이 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Aftershocks can follow a strong earthquake.
Relief supplies arrived in the area hit by the strong earthquake.
Many people lost their homes in the strong earthquake.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 강진 소식을 계속 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The news kept reporting about the strong earthquake.

examples.ko: 전문가는 강진에 대비해 건물을 튼튼하게 지어야 한다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The expert said buildings must be built strong to prepare for strong earthquakes.

explain: 강진은 규모가 큰 지진이에요. 더 큰 피해를 주는 지진은 '대지진'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '규모 6의 강진'처럼 숫자와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: A strong earthquake occurred near the sea last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 큰 지진이 일어났다고 전할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for a big earthquake happening.

phrases.en: We helped the people hurt by the strong earthquake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지진으로 입은 피해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to damage caused by the earthquake.

phrases.en: A magnitude 7 strong earthquake shook the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자와 함께 지진의 크기를 말하는 뉴스 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news expression that gives the magnitude of the quake.

explain_en: 강진 is an earthquake of large magnitude. One causing even greater damage is a 대지진. In the news it is paired with a number, like 규모 6의 강진 (a magnitude 6 strong earthquake).

examples.en: In spring I sneeze because of pollen.
Pollen blew in the wind and piled up on the car.
Pollen can cause allergies.
Bees collect pollen and carry it home.
People sensitive to pollen wear masks.
The weather news reports the pollen level too.

explain: 봄에 '꽃가루 알레르기'나 '꽃가루 농도'처럼 건강과 날씨 이야기에서 같이 들어요. 한자어로는 '화분'이라고도 하는데, '화분'은 꽃을 심은 그릇도 가리켜서 헷갈릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I have a pollen allergy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄에 건강 이야기를 할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in spring health talk.

phrases.en: The wind is blowing and pollen is flying around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공기 중에 꽃가루가 떠다니는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes pollen floating in the air.

phrases.en: The pollen level is high today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 예보에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in weather reports.

explain_en: You hear it with health and weather topics in spring, like '꽃가루 알레르기' (pollen allergy) or '꽃가루 농도' (pollen count). The Sino-Korean word is '화분', but that also means a flowerpot, so it can be confusing.

en: water of a stream; water of a brook

examples.en: Children are splashing around in the clear stream.
It rained, so the stream swelled a lot.
Hearing the sound of a stream calms my mind.
In summer we play with our feet in the stream.
I walked up along the stream for a good while.
This stream doesn't dry up even in winter.

explain: '시냇물'이라고도 해요. 강보다 작고 졸졸 흐르는 물을 떠올리면 돼요. 비슷한 말로 '개울'이 있어요.

phrases.en: Hearing the sound of the stream calms me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냇물'과 같은 말이에요. 노래나 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as '냇물'; it often appears in songs and stories.

phrases.en: A stream flows beside the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 흐르는 모습을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for describing flowing water.

phrases.en: It was hot, so I dipped my feet in the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 냇가에서 쉬는 장면에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for relaxing by a stream in summer.
phrases.en_equiv: to soak one's feet in the stream

explain_en: It is also called '시냇물'. Think of a small, trickling flow of water, smaller than a river. A similar word is '개울'.

examples.en: A welcome rain finally fell after a long time.
The farmers waited for the welcome rain.
Thanks to the rain, the fields came back to life.
The rain that fell last night was really welcome.
The news reported rain coming tomorrow.
The trees turned green with the rain.

explain: 그냥 '비'가 아니라 오래 가물 때 내리는 반가운 비를 '단비'라고 해요. 비가 오면 불편한 사람도 많아서, 기다리던 비일 때만 이 말을 써요. '단'은 '달다'와 같은 뜻이라서 비가 달게 느껴진다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 바쁠 때 친구가 도와줘서 가뭄에 단비 같았어요.
phrases.en: rain in a drought
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 필요한 때에 받은 도움이나 좋은 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes help or good news that arrives exactly when it is badly needed.

explain_en: 단비 is the welcome rain that falls after a long dry spell. It is only used when people were waiting for the rain. The 단 is the same as in 달다 (sweet), so the rain feels sweet.

examples.en: A big earthquake happened in Japan.
A big earthquake comes suddenly, at any time.
That city went through a big earthquake long ago.
We prepare water and food for a big earthquake.
Many houses collapsed in the big earthquake.
A big earthquake is scary, but a tsunami is scarier.

explain: '지진' 앞에 '대'가 붙은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '큰 지진'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 뉴스에서는 '강진'이라는 말도 나와요.

phrases.en: A big earthquake happened last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대지진'을 쉽게 풀어서 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way of saying 'daejijin'.

phrases.en: An earthquake happened in that city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지진이 일어났다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say an earthquake occurred.

phrases.en: The damage from the great earthquake was very large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지진 때문에 입은 피해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for damage caused by the earthquake.

explain_en: It is '지진' with '대' (big) in front. In daily talk people often just say '큰 지진'. The news also uses '강진' (strong quake).

examples.ko: 불이 나서 모두 건물 밖으로 대피했어요.
examples.en: A fire broke out, so everyone evacuated the building.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오기 전에 안전한 곳으로 대피하세요.
examples.en: Take shelter somewhere safe before the typhoon arrives.

examples.ko: 지진이 나면 책상 밑으로 먼저 대피해요.
examples.en: When an earthquake hits, we first take cover under a desk.
Residents are evacuating to the school gym.

examples.ko: 아이들은 선생님과 함께 천천히 대피할 거예요.
examples.en: The children will evacuate slowly with their teacher.

examples.ko: 홍수 때문에 대피한 사람들이 아직 집에 못 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: The people who evacuated because of the flood still can't go back home.

explain: '피하다'는 싫은 사람이나 일을 피할 때도 쓰지만, '대피하다'는 재난이나 위험 때문에 안전한 곳으로 몸을 옮길 때만 써요. 보통 '~(으)로 대피하다' 모양이고, 뉴스와 안내 방송에서 아주 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: An earthquake hit, so we took shelter in the school playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디로 몸을 옮겼는지 '~(으)로'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~(으)로' to say where you moved to safety.

phrases.en: Where is the nearest shelter?
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난 때 사람들이 피하는 안전한 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A safe place where people go during a disaster.

phrases.en: When the evacuation announcement comes on, go out right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험할 때 건물이나 지역에서 나오는 안내 방송이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The announcement made when people must evacuate.

explain_en: 피하다 can mean avoiding a person or a task, but 대피하다 is only for moving to a safe place because of a disaster or danger. It usually appears as '~(으)로 대피하다' and is very common in news and emergency announcements.

t90.ax: Residents are evacuating to the school gym.

examples.en: Great floods often appear in old tales.
Last summer, the village was flooded by a great flood.

examples.ko: 대홍수 때문에 많은 사람이 집을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their homes because of the great flood.
I saw news about the great flood on TV.

examples.ko: 그 강은 대홍수를 몇 번 겪었어요.
examples.en: That river has been through great floods several times.

examples.ko: 대홍수 뒤에 복구 작업이 한참 이어졌어요.
examples.en: After the great flood, the recovery work went on for a long time.

explain: '홍수'보다 규모가 아주 큰 홍수예요. 뉴스, 옛이야기, 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 평소 비가 많이 와서 길이 잠기는 정도는 그냥 '홍수'나 '침수'라고 해요.

phrases.en: A great flood happened in that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 큰 홍수가 생겼다는 뉴스나 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news or stories about a very big flood happening.

phrases.example: 그 마을은 몇 년 전에 대홍수를 겪었어요.
phrases.en: That village went through a great flood a few years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 지역이 큰 피해를 직접 경험했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people or a region directly experienced a big flood.
phrases.en_equiv: to go through a great flood

phrases.en: I read a story about a great flood in a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기나 신화 속 홍수를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for floods in old tales or myths.

explain_en: It is a flood on a much larger scale than '홍수'. It often appears in news, old tales and history. When heavy rain just floods roads, people usually say plain '홍수' or '침수'.

examples.en: My umbrella flipped inside out because of the gust.
A sudden gust blew and my hat flew off.
The forecast said to watch out for gusts in the afternoon.
The child frightened by the gust started crying.
A rookie who appeared out of nowhere won the title.
The sign shook even in a light gust.

explain: 갑자기 세게 불다가 그치는 바람이에요. '태풍'은 열대 바다에서 생겨 큰 비와 함께 오는 큰 폭풍이고, '돌풍'은 짧고 갑작스러운 바람이에요. 뉴스에서는 사람이나 작품이 갑자기 큰 인기를 얻을 때도 '돌풍'을 써요.

phrases.en: cause a sensation
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 큰 인기나 화제를 모은다는 뜻이에요. 드라마, 가수, 상품에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to suddenly gain great popularity or attention. It is used often for dramas, singers, and products.

explain_en: It is a wind that blows hard suddenly and then stops. A '태풍' is a big storm that forms over tropical seas and brings heavy rain, while a '돌풍' is a short, abrupt wind. In the news, '돌풍' is also used when a person or a work suddenly becomes hugely popular.

examples.en: When the whale breathed, a column of water shot up.
The fountain shot a tall column of water into the air.

examples.ko: 소방차 호스에서 물기둥처럼 물이 뿜어져 나왔어요.
examples.en: Water burst out of the fire truck's hose like a pillar.
A rainbow appeared between the columns of water.
The children played happily under the columns of water.
The column of water was as tall as a building.

explain: 굵고 높게 솟아오르는 물줄기를 말해요. 가늘게 흐르는 '물줄기'와 달리 고래, 분수, 부딪히는 파도처럼 힘 있게 솟는 모습에 어울려요.

phrases.en: A huge column of water shot up above the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 힘 있게 위로 올라가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water rising up forcefully.

phrases.en: The whale spouted a column of water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고래나 분수가 물을 뿜을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for whales or fountains spraying water.

phrases.en: A tall column of water came out of the fountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 꾸며 주는 말을 붙여 크기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A describing word before it shows the size.

explain_en: It describes a thick, tall jet of water rising up. Unlike the thin flowing '물줄기', it suits powerful scenes like whales, fountains and crashing waves.

examples.en: This neighborhood suffers flooding every rainy season.
There was flooding because of the rain yesterday.
The underground parking lot was a mess because of the flood.
School was closed because of the flooding.
Luckily, no one was hurt despite the flooding.
Volunteers gathered at the flood site.

explain: 큰비 때문에 생기는 홍수 피해뿐 아니라, 집 안에 수도관이 터져 물바다가 되는 일에도 써요. '물난리가 나다', '물난리를 겪다'처럼 말하고, '수해'보다 편한 말투예요.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 지하철역에 물난리가 났어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so the subway station flooded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 물 피해가 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when water damage suddenly happens.

phrases.en: Our neighborhood suffered flooding last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 직접 경험했다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that someone experienced the damage firsthand.

phrases.example: 이번 수해로 많은 집이 피해를 입었어요.
phrases.en: Many houses were damaged by this flood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물난리'보다 딱딱한 말이라 뉴스나 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than 물난리, common in news and writing.

explain_en: It covers flood damage from heavy rain, and also a home flooded by a burst pipe. It is said as '물난리가 나다' or '물난리를 겪다', and sounds more casual than '수해'.

t90.ax: Volunteers gathered at the flood site.

en: force of flowing water; speed of flowing water

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the current got stronger.
Swimming against the current is really hard.

examples.ko: 이 강은 물살이 느려서 배 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This river has a slow current, so it's good for boating.
The child almost got swept away by the current.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 물살 소리가 시원하게 들려요.
examples.en: The sound of the rushing water under the bridge is refreshing.

examples.ko: 낚시꾼이 빠른 물살을 피해 자리를 잡았어요.
examples.en: The angler picked a spot away from the fast current.

explain: '물살'은 흐르는 물의 힘과 빠르기에 초점이 있어서 '물살이 세다', '빠르다', '느리다'로 말해요. 가만히 있는 물에는 쓰지 않아요. 바다에서 크게 일어나는 움직임은 '파도'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This river has a fast current, so it's dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 흐르는 속도를 말할 때 '빠르다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 빠르다 to describe how fast the water flows.

phrases.en: The current is slow, so it's good for boating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠르다'의 반대로, 물이 천천히 흐를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 빠르다, for slowly flowing water.

phrases.en: A small leaf follows the current.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물살을 거슬러'와 반대로 흐름을 따라 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of going against the current; moving along with the flow.

explain_en: '물살' focuses on the force and speed of moving water, so you say '물살이 세다/빠르다/느리다'. It is not used for still water. The big motions at sea are called '파도' (waves).

examples.en: At high tide the tidal flat is covered by water.
We have to go back before the tide comes in.
Today's high tide is around three in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 밀물과 썰물은 하루에 두 번씩 있어요.
examples.en: There are two high tides and two low tides a day.
The boat came into the harbor on the rising tide.
At rush hour people surged in like a tide.

explain: 반대말은 '썰물'이고, 둘이 같이 '밀물과 썰물'로 자주 나와요. 바닷물이 들어오는 때를 말해요. 사람이나 물건이 한꺼번에 몰려오는 모습을 '밀물처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 바다에서는 하루에 밀물과 썰물이 두 번씩 있어요.
phrases.en: At the sea, there are two high tides and two low tides a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 말이 짝으로 가장 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words most often appear as a pair.

phrases.en: On the first day of the sale, customers poured in like a tide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 한꺼번에 많이 올 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for many people or things arriving at once.
phrases.en_equiv: to flood in like the tide

phrases.example: 갯벌에 가기 전에 밀물 시간을 확인하세요.
phrases.en: Check the high tide time before going to the tidal flat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다에 가기 전에 확인하는 정보로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Information people often check before going to the sea.

explain_en: The opposite is '썰물', and the two often appear together as '밀물과 썰물'. It means the time when seawater flows in. You can also say '밀물처럼' figuratively for people or things pouring in all at once.
